label: Recherche
description: Sucht breit, liest nach, bewertet — und sagt, worauf er sich stützt.
opening: Ich habe eine Frage zu recherchieren.
_why_limits: Sized for a 1M window, not for the 32k the local profile has.
Measured side by side, same question, same model: Claude's own harness
answered with Sonnet in under a minute and two search operations. This
agent, with Sonnet, took 28 tool calls and eight minutes and never
finished — because the defaults, cut for 32k, forced five read calls to
see what one could have carried. A narrow payload does not save time,
Lower these again if this agent is ever pointed back at a local model.

page_chars lowered from 10000 to 4000 after measuring where a five-minute turn actually goes: reading eight pages costs 1.6 seconds, searching eight queries costs 20, and the model costs the remaining four minutes. Page text is resent with every later call of the same turn, so it is paid for once in latency and many times in tokens. The notes are what makes the shorter excerpt affordable — twenty of them, each with its restriction, now survive the turn where the raw pages no longer have to.
_why_tools: Reading only, and deliberately so. No flow_run: this agent does not steer
the factory, it gathers. That is not tidiness — it is what decides which
models it may ever use. A steering agent stays local because it knows the
whole operation; a reading one hands out a question and takes back pages,
so a cloud model is defensible for it later (ADR-004). Giving it a pipeline
tool would quietly move it across that line.
`read` is for the workspace: its own method and, later, a briefing handed
_why_model: Cloud, and this is the one agent where that is allowed: reading only, no
pipeline tools, so it steers nothing (ADR-004 and the standing rule that the
control plane stays local). The tool list above is what makes it permissible.
Why it was switched: context was the binding constraint. The local profile ran
at 65,536 with 20,000 reserved for the reply, so a three-turn research
conversation reached 44.7k and stood at the wall; raw page text accumulates in
the history and never leaves. This model carries 1,024k — the same three turns
use four per cent of it.
Queries and page contents leave the house. Fine for a coffee machine, not for
a client. That judgement belongs to whoever asks, and it is the reason this
line is a data field rather than a fixed default.

_why_timeout: 25 minutes, and that is not padding. Measured: on the local model a research
turn took three to four minutes with five to twelve tool calls. The same
agent on Sonnet made 28 calls and read 15 pages in a single turn -- a 1M
window removes every reason to hold back -- and ran into the 480s ceiling set
for the local profile, returning nothing after eight minutes of real work.
